name: Huperzine A
lead: Huperzine A is a plant alkaloid isolated from the Chinese club moss Huperzia serrata and a potent, reversible inhibitor of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase, which breaks down acetylcholine [1][2]. Grokipedia states that it has been approved as a prescription drug for Alzheimer's disease in China since 1996 and is sold elsewhere as a dietary supplement [1].

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed mainly in height-maxxing, where some guides pair it with growth-hormone secretagogues on the theory that it lowers somatostatin and so raises growth hormone [3][4]. Other forum users dispute this theory, saying they found no study linking huperzine A to somatostatin inhibition or height [4].
No published human trial has tested huperzine A for height or any other appearance outcome. Clinical research has concentrated on Alzheimer's disease and cognition [5][6][7].
infobox: Oral (supplement); injection formulations in clinical research [8]
Approved in China for Alzheimer's disease, per Grokipedia [1]

paras: Huperzine A belongs to the Lycopodium alkaloids, a group of more than 200 alkaloids from club mosses, several of which inhibit acetylcholinesterase [9]. Grokipedia describes the traditional use of Huperzia serrata in Chinese medicine for bruises, swelling and rheumatism, and notes that the plant is slow-growing and wild harvesting raises sustainability concerns [1].

A 2006 review described huperzine A as a highly specific, reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor with better blood-brain barrier penetration, higher oral bioavailability and longer action than tacrine, donepezil and rivastigmine, and with protective effects on cells in animal models [2]. The crystal structure of acetylcholinesterase bound to huperzine A was published in 1997 [10]. A 2017 review discusses it among traditional Chinese medicine ingredients studied for anti-ageing effects [11].

Registered trials have tested huperzine A in Alzheimer's disease, including a US phase 2 trial of 150 participants and a Chinese phase 2/3 trial of sustained-release tablets with 390 participants [5][6]. Other registered studies cover schizophrenia with cognitive impairment, traumatic brain injury, cocaine dependence, cognition during exercise, presbycusis and pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers [7][8][12][13][14][15]. Grokipedia summarises meta-analyses as reporting improvements in cognition and daily living in Alzheimer's disease, with mild side effects such as nausea and dizziness [1]. No studies were found testing huperzine A for height, growth hormone or appearance.

A looksmax.org thread documented a teenager's planned multi-month height-maxxing regimen combining a growth-hormone secretagogue with huperzine A; another user answered that such threads rarely deliver the promised updates [3]. A second thread argued that the somatostatin-inhibition claim had been attributed to huperzine A in a popular height guide in error, confusing it with pyridostigmine, and said the author could find no study linking the two [4]. One reply proposed a chain through acetylcholine and somatostatin as a possible but uncertain mechanism [4].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org huperzine A is discussed in height-maxxing threads as a growth-hormone aid [3][4].

claims.claim: Huperzine A is a somatostatin inhibitor that raises growth hormone and could add height.
claims.believers: A popular height-maxxing guide and some users pair it with a secretagogue for this reason, and one teenager planned a six-month regimen aiming to gain several centimetres [3].
claims.experts: Published work describes huperzine A as an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor [2]. No studies were found showing that it inhibits somatostatin or affects height.

claims.claim: The somatostatin claim is a mix-up with pyridostigmine, so huperzine A does nothing for height.
claims.believers: One forum poster said he found no study linking huperzine A to somatostatin and that the idea came from confusion with pyridostigmine; another called it 'cope' [4].
claims.experts: The pharmacology literature describes direct acetylcholinesterase inhibition and cognitive research [2][9]; no height studies were found.

claims.claim: Raising acetylcholine indirectly lowers somatostatin and so could raise growth hormone.
claims.believers: A reply in a debate thread outlined this chain as a slight possibility while expressing uncertainty [4].
claims.experts: No published studies in the sources reviewed test this chain for huperzine A in humans.

card.summary: Club-moss cholinesterase inhibitor sold as a nootropic and floated in height-maxxing; no height study exists.
card.note: Forum height claims rest on an unconfirmed somatostatin theory; clinical work is on Alzheimer's disease.

quick.overview:
Huperzine A is an alkaloid from Chinese club moss that inhibits acetylcholinesterase. It is a prescription drug for Alzheimer's disease in China and a supplement elsewhere.

On looksmax.org it is discussed for height-maxxing via a theory that it raises growth hormone. No study has tested it for height, and forum users themselves dispute the theory.
quick.mechanism: It blocks acetylcholinesterase, raising acetylcholine levels in the brain. The forum theory that it also inhibits somatostatin was not found in the studies reviewed.
quick.risks: Grokipedia lists mild nausea, dizziness and insomnia and possible interactions with other cholinesterase inhibitors or anticholinergic drugs. It is sold as a supplement in the US.
